column1: # Formula cases with the result Excel gives, and where that result comes from.
# Columns (tab-separated): formula · expected · source. Expected: a number, "text" (quotes
# doubled inside), TRUE/FALSE or an error such as #NUM!. Read by formula::tests::excel_cases.
#   ms:<function>   the examples in Microsoft's documentation of that function
#                   (a rate is the same whatever the unit of the cash flows: the scaled cases)
#   ms:precision    Excel keeps 15 significant digits and rounds the decimal it shows
#                   these follow from it and are widely reported results, not yet executed in Excel by us
#   excel:accounting  Excel's built-in Accounting format code; a "*" fill has no width in TEXT
# ---- 2.7 IRR / XIRR / RATE convergence (review 11 Oct). Microsoft shows these rounded; the
# formulas round the same way (Excel stops XIRR at 1E-6 %: its 0.373362535 is not the exact root
# 0.3733625335…, so XIRR is compared at the 37.34 % it shows). Dates are serials: 39448 = 1 Jan 2008 … 39904 = 1 Apr 2009.
# the same flows scaled by 1E-12 … 1E9 give the same rate (a rate does not depend on the currency unit)
# ---- 2.9 Excel-verified cases for eval.rs (review 11 Oct). Each is an example from the Microsoft page
# of the function (ms:<function>); dates are compared with DATE() so no serial is typed by hand.
# ms:leapyear  "Excel incorrectly assumes that the year 1900 is a leap year"
#              serial 60 is 29 Feb 1900, serial 1 is 1 Jan 1900, and weekdays before March 1900 follow the serial.
